summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia was admitted for recurrent substernal chest pain radiating to both shoulders, associated with dizziness and shortness of breath. The pain resolved with sublingual nitroglycerin and aspirin in the field. Initial evaluation showed hyperglycemia (glucose 408) but no acute ischemic changes on EKG or elevated cardiac enzymes, ruling out myocardial infarction. She had increasing exertional angina over recent months but remained stable during admission. Her medications were adjusted: lisinopril and simvastatin doses increased, metoprolol switched back to succinate formulation, and isosorbide mononitrate started for angina prophylaxis. Metformin was held initially but restarted at discharge. She also reported dysuria, flank pain, and productive cough, which were noted for outpatient follow-up. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to monitor symptoms and follow up with her primary and cardiac care providers.
